newsitem.title: USA: USWC light crudes firm with fading March WTI trade.
newsitem.headline: USWC light crudes firm with fading March WTI trade.

text.p: Outright prices for U.S. West Coast light crudes edged up with a higher WTI/Cushing market, but the basis for Alaska North Slope ANS) grade was in dispute as March WTI business ended, traders said.
BP, the main producer of ANS, said it would consider selling March barrels off a March or April WTI basis.
But a company trader declined to make an offer, prompting buyers to put their bids at $1.60 under April WTI, which had ranged as much as 30 cents a barrel lower than outight March WTI last Friday.
BP said they saw ANS at $1.10 off March WTI.
Traders said Line 63 prices stood unchanged at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05, with the WTI-based market assessed at minus $1.95 to minus $1.85 under WTI.
Kern River heavy crude was steady Tuesday, a day after major oil companies dropped their postings for California grades 75 cents a barrel.
Outright prices ranged 13.84/14.04 a barrel,traders said, with rumors that an extra 5,000 to 10,000 bpd of heavies were moving east over the All-American pipeline.
